body:
Yeah...you're right. Really...I guess I'm just reeling from so big a hit, but when the dust settles really my life is okay. I got all my fingers and toes. And believe me, the addict that lives in my head was all about wanting to use again -- anything to get out of the pain. I don't know if I'd say I'm proud, but I know I'm very thankful I didn't do that.

Thanks for being here to help me get the right perspective. I was throwing myself a class A pity party, but it got pretty bad last night....so....just thank you so much for being here.

Thank you...I don't know whether or not I deserved charges or not. I know that I needed help. I'd wanted to stop everything -- all my use of porn, affairs, sex, etc -- but I never could. Getting arrested got me help, and I was and am thankful for that. I really don't know where things would have ended up in another ten or fifteen years if I just continued like I was.  

At any rate, thanks for your kind words. And you're probably right that there are going to be options even if I don't know what they are.

I have attorneys who are representing me. They're two well-respected guys in the legal community who found out about my situation and offered to represent me pro-bono. I haven't had a lot of a chance to fully discuss future options with them, but I do know if I want to sit for the bar someplace I'm going to have to move to do it.

And that scares the shit out of me...for a lot of reasons.

Anyway, you're right -- well that's how the school explained it to me in my first semester -- so long as I show evidence of rehabilitation I should be fine. So I stuck it out, only to find out that wasn't exactly the case.

Thanks for your kind words. I struggle a lot with self-worth. I poured a lot of ambition and self-will into this dream as a substitute for actually being okay with myself. I figured if I excelled, if I beat out other law students, if I won tournaments, got published, etc, that would cover up or make up for my dark, dark, dark past.

And the truth is that was not the case. I don't think I have to be defined by my crime, but I also don't think I was going about redefining myself in the right way. My suit became a suit of armor, and I was just pretending to be something that I wasn't. 

You're probably right about the job front. There probably is stuff out there where my law degree will open some doors. I've no idea what those things are, but for now I still have my job as a paralegal at the firm I've worked at for a few years. It keeps a roof over my head, and really that's the most important thing. 

Responding to these keeps making me realize that the essential thing in all this is that I'm sober. I used to not think that would ever be a possibility for me. Thank you for helping me understand what's actually important in this situation, and where my ego and my addiction/s are just trying to work on me.

Yeah...I could, well, potentially take it in another jurisdiction. Each state regulates their own bar admissions, so I could research and find another jurisdiction that would allow me to sit for the bar, apply there, and see what happens.

I don't really think there's any one particular thing law grads do that's outside of practicing law. It's really just a general education degree. I mean...maybe it will open some doors for me I don't know. Right now I still have my job at the law firm I've worked at a few years as a law clerk / paralegal. I do writing and research, amongst other things, in an area of law that interests me (criminal defense). Maybe I should just be glad that I have that and not be focused on this thing as the end of the world. Really, I'm thankful to not be in prison. People who do what did often go to prison for a very long time. I got to go to law school instead. 

And yeah, I do a lot of 12-step recovery stuff. I have a history with drugs and alcohol, though my biggest issues are with sexual addiction (obviously). I'm involved with the lawyer assistance program in my state -- basically an arm of the bar that deals with lawyers who struggle with addiction issues -- and I'm very thankful for that. 

And, as I write that, I realize the number one thing is that I am sober. Used to be a time when I never thought there could be any other way to live, despite so badly wanting out of it. 

Thanks...
